module_description: Azure service status: your subscription's Service Health (ARM Resource Health) plus the public Azure status feed.

hints.tenant_id: Entra ID directory (tenant) ID of the app registration.
hints.client_id: Application (client) ID of the app registration.
hints.client_secret: Client secret of the app registration.
hints.subscription_id: Azure subscription to read Service Health from. The app needs an Azure RBAC role assignment (Reader is enough) ON THIS SUBSCRIPTION — an Entra app role does not grant it.
hints.check_service_health: Reads Microsoft.ResourceHealth events: outages, planned maintenance and advisories affecting YOUR resources and regions.
hints.health_window_hours: Only consider events updated within this many hours.
hints.check_public_status: Reads the public Azure status feed. Needs no credentials, but only reports globally announced incidents — it cannot tell whether your resources are affected.
hints.public_filter: Only report entries mentioning this text (e.g. 'West Europe' or 'Storage'). Blank = every entry.
hints.check_resource_health: Azure's own health view of every resource in the subscription — VMs, VPN gateways, networks, databases and anything else. One result per unhealthy resource. Needs the app to have Reader on the subscription.
hints.resource_filter: Only watch resources whose id contains this text — a type ('virtualMachines'), a resource group ('/rg-prod/') or a name. Blank = every resource in the subscription.
hints.resource_list: Report one result per resource, healthy ones included, so the section lists the whole subscription instead of only what is broken. A large subscription turns this into hundreds of stored results and history rows.
hints.check_vm_power: Whether the VMs are actually running. Resource Health cannot answer this: a deallocated VM reports Unknown, the same as a resource Azure has no opinion about.
hints.vm_filter: Which VMs both VM checks look at: a resource group ('/rg-prod/') or a name. Blank = every VM in the subscription.
hints.check_quotas: Subscription quota headroom (vCPUs, public IPs, disks), so running out shows up here instead of failing a deployment.
hints.quota_region: Quotas are per region. ARM wants the resource-id form (westeurope), not the display name - use the picker.
hints.quota_pct: Report a quota once it reaches this share of its limit. At 100% it is an error, not a warning: the next deployment will fail.
hints.check_app_secrets: App-registration secrets and certificates about to expire - including ServiceSentry's own, which nothing else would notice. Needs the Graph permission Application.Read.All (re-run the wizard's 'fix permissions' on an app created before this check existed).
hints.secret_days: Report a credential this many days before it expires.
hints.vm_list: Report one result per VM, running ones included, so the section lists the machines instead of one total. On by default: the power state of each machine is the point of this check.
hints.check_vm_metrics: CPU and disk saturation per running VM, from Azure Monitor. Only what Azure reports WITHOUT an agent - disk SPACE and guest memory are not available here at all; use the filesystem and RAM modules over SSH for those.
hints.cpu_pct: Report a VM whose average CPU over the window reaches this. Blank = do not check CPU.
hints.disk_pct: Report a VM whose OS or data disk reaches this share of its provisioned IOPS - the throttling that makes a machine feel broken while every health check stays green. Blank = do not check disks.
hints.metric_window: Average the metrics over this many minutes. Longer ignores brief spikes; shorter reacts sooner.
hints.check_budgets: Spend against the subscription's Azure budgets. In Azure the thing that hurts is rarely an outage - it is the invoice, and it is the one number the person paying asks about. Needs a budget to exist in Azure; the Reader role already covers reading it.
hints.budget_pct: Report a budget once the spend reaches this share of it. Over 100% is an error, not a warning: that money is already spent. A budget FORECAST to be exceeded is always reported, whatever this is set to.

messages.az_no_creds: tenant_id, client_id, client_secret and subscription_id are required

messages.az_public_fail: Could not read the public Azure status feed: {}
messages.az_public_ok: No open entries in the public Azure status feed
messages.az_public_open: {} entries in the public Azure status feed — latest: {}
messages.az_quota_no_region: Pick the region whose quotas to check
messages.az_quota_empty: No quota reported for the region: {}
messages.az_sec_fail: Could not read the app registrations: {}
messages.az_sec_ok: None of the {} credentials expires within {} days
messages.az_met_no_threshold: Set a CPU or disk threshold for this check to do anything
messages.az_met_ok: The {} running VMs are below their thresholds ({} min average)
messages.az_res_nohealth: {} exists (Azure reports no health for this type)
messages.az_bud_none: This subscription has no budget - nothing is watching the spend
